name: ContextObjects RPS
summary: Dual-collection Reversed-Path Search for multi-industry semantic object instances. Full objects in context_objects, denormalised path→value pairs in context_objects_search for fast AQL queries. No dictionaries — meaning lives in the model schema.
description: Stores ContextObject instances using the Reversed-Path Search dual-collection layout adapted for multi-industry semantic models. Every data point carries a unique node ID. Instances are queried via an AQL dialect that compiles to MongoDB aggregation pipelines targeting the search collection with compound indexes on sn.nid and sn.v.

strategy.description: Collection names, field shorthands, and query limits

index_contract.summary: Required MongoDB indexes are declared in the strategy spec with logical field aliases. Runtime plan/apply resolves collection names and field shorthands from the active environment config.

ui.story:
Any team that works with structured semantic data faces the same tension: record-level operations need the full object, while population-level queries need to scan across thousands of records efficiently. Traditional document stores force you to choose — either keep complete records and accept slow cross-record searches, or flatten everything into rows and lose the richness of your model.

ContextObjects RPS solves this with a dual-collection layout that serves both workloads simultaneously. The primary collection holds every instance exactly as created, making individual record retrieval instant. The search collection maintains a compact, denormalised view of every path→value pair across all instances, enabling sub-millisecond AQL queries over large populations.

Because semantic meaning lives entirely in the model schema — not in dictionaries, not in code tables — the system works for any domain. A clinical trial schema, a financial instrument definition, a supply chain event model: each produces the same dual-collection layout, queried by the same AQL syntax.
ui.how_it_works:
On ingest, the strategy validates the instance against its semantic model schema, then walks the data tree to extract every node along its path. The primary document is written to context_objects with the full content nodes array (cn). A denormalised projection is written in parallel to context_objects_search — one entry per leaf node in the sn array, each carrying its path, nodeId, value, and dataType.

At query time, AQL compiles to a MongoDB aggregation pipeline. The objectType predicate is hoisted to a top-level $match for index coverage. Remaining WHERE clauses become $elemMatch conditions on the sn array, matched by nodeId for precision or by path for hierarchy traversal. The pipeline is always targeted at context_objects_search — the primary collection is never touched by queries.
benefits: Domain-agnostic — the same layout works for any industry vertical. No clinical vocabulary required.
Dual-collection layout gives sub-millisecond path queries at scale without sacrificing record completeness.
No dictionaries and no code tables — semantic meaning lives in the model schema, which means zero bootstrap overhead on activation.
AQL syntax mirrors the openEHR AQL dialect so teams already familiar with it can query immediately.
Instances are first-class records: generate, validate, ingest, query, and export them independently of the model.
Compound indexes on sn.nid+sn.v and sn.p+sn.v are declared in the spec and applied automatically on plan/apply.
ui.ideal_for: Any domain with explicit semantic models where node IDs are stable and you need fast path-based queries across large populations. Particularly well suited for clinical trial data, IoT telemetry with structured schemas, financial instrument lifecycle events, and supply chain object tracking.
consider_alternatives: If your data is clinical EHR archetypes (openEHR), use openehr.rps_dual instead — it includes dictionary compression and Atlas Search support.
If your data is HL7 FHIR R5 resources, use fhir.clinical_cdr instead.
If you only need record-level lookups and never query across instances, a single-collection layout is simpler.

cards.title: AQL Queries
cards.body: WHERE clauses compile to $elemMatch on the sn array. objectType is hoisted to a top-level $match for index coverage.

cards.title: Dual-Collection Ingest
cards.body: Every instance writes to context_objects (full cn[]) and context_objects_search (flat sn[]) in a single operation.

cards.title: Zero Bootstrap
cards.body: No dictionaries, no code tables. Activation creates two collections and their indexes — nothing else.
